title: Event Triggering via innerHTML
description: The URL fragment is reflected into the page via innerHTML with no re-render on user action. Because there is no click, focus, or other user interaction available to a passive scanner, the payload's event handler must be one that fires automatically the moment it is inserted into the DOM.
objectives: Notice the sink re-renders on hashchange, but nothing on the page requires a click or focus to reach a script-executing element.
Recognize that onclick/onfocus-style payloads will sit inert forever without simulated user interaction.
Deliver a payload whose event fires automatically on insertion/parse (no interaction needed) to prove script execution.
hints: <script> tags are inert when inserted via innerHTML — this sink needs an HTML element with a self-firing event handler instead.
SVG's onload handler fires as soon as the element is parsed by the DOM, with no click needed: <svg onload=alert(document.domain)>
also autofires because the broken src triggers the error event immediately.
<details open ontoggle=alert(document.domain)> is another zero-interaction trigger, useful when onerror/onload are filtered.
Set the URL fragment and let the page re-render, e.g. location.hash = '<svg onload=alert(document.domain)>'
